board_events.text: Test the assertion: Fabaceae stamens are indeed diadelphous. TRUE.
Test the reason: 'diadelphous' here means a nine-plus-one arrangement, nine fused and one free. The reason states exactly this. TRUE.
And it is the DEFINITION underlying the assertion, so it explains it. Answer: (a).
When a reason is the definition of the term in the assertion, it is always the correct explanation.

segments.text: Fourth example, and it is the high-difficulty assertion-reason. It is also the cleanest illustration of what these items are actually testing.
The assertion says that in Fabaceae the androecium is described as diadelphous. The reason says nine stamens are fused by their filaments into one bundle while the tenth remains free.
Test the assertion first. Are Fabaceae stamens diadelphous? Yes. That is the family's signature word, and we anchored it two sections ago. The assertion is true.
Now test the reason. Look at the board. Nine fused into one bundle, one free. Is that what diadelphous means here?
Yes. Di-adelphous means two bundles, and in Fabaceae the two bundles are nine and one. The reason states exactly this. So the reason is true.

And now the deciding question. Is the reason why the assertion holds? Look at what the reason actually is. It is not a separate fact that happens to support the assertion. It is the definition of the word in the assertion.
So it explains it in the strongest possible way. The answer is option (a).

<whisper>And take the general rule out of this, because it will save you time in the hall. When a reason is the definition of the term used in the assertion, it is always the correct explanation. You do not need to think further. You have already finished.
चौथा example, और ये high-difficulty assertion-reason है। और ये सबसे साफ़ मिसाल भी है कि ये items असल में जाँच क्या रहे हैं।
Assertion कहता है कि Fabaceae में androecium को diadelphous कहा जाता है। Reason कहता है कि नौ stamens अपने filaments से जुड़कर एक bundle बनाते हैं, जबकि दसवाँ आज़ाद रहता है।
पहले assertion test कीजिए। क्या Fabaceae के stamens diadelphous हैं? हाँ। यही तो इस family का signature शब्द है, और हमने उसे दो sections पहले anchor किया था। Assertion true है।
अब reason test कीजिए। Board देखिए। नौ जुड़कर एक bundle, एक आज़ाद। क्या यहाँ diadelphous का यही मतलब है?
हाँ। Di-adelphous यानी दो bundles, और Fabaceae में वो दो bundles हैं नौ और एक। Reason ठीक यही कह रहा है। तो reason true है।

और अब वो सवाल जो faisla करता है। क्या यही वजह है कि assertion टिकता है? देखिए reason असल में है क्या। ये कोई अलग fact नहीं है जो संयोग से assertion का साथ दे रहा हो। ये उसी शब्द की definition है जो assertion में है।
तो ये उसे सबसे मज़बूत तरीक़े से explain करता है। जवाब है option (a)।

<whisper>और इससे general rule निकाल लीजिए, क्योंकि ये exam hall में आपका समय बचाएगा। जब reason उसी term की definition हो जो assertion में इस्तेमाल हुआ है, तो वो हमेशा सही explanation होता है। आगे सोचने की ज़रूरत नहीं। आप पहले ही ख़त्म कर चुके हैं।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for families and descriptions

board_events.text: Five pitfalls, and two habits for the last mile
Pitfall one, mixing the three formulae. Anchor one signature word per family: Fabaceae = diadelphous / papilionaceous; Solanaceae = epipetalous / berry; Liliaceae = tepals / epiphyllous.
Pitfall two, perianth versus calyx plus corolla. Liliaceae has ONE undifferentiated whorl, tepals, not separate K and C.
Pitfall three, phylloclade versus phyllode. Phylloclade = modified STEM (Opuntia). Phyllode = modified petiole or leaf (Acacia). Same green flattened look, different organ.
Pitfall four: 'complete' counts whorls (four present); 'tri- or tetra- or penta-merous' counts parts per whorl. Independent ideas.
Pitfall five, description out of order. Always habit, then vegetative, then floral, then fruit and seed. Per-field marking punishes a scrambled answer.
Pro-tip: for any 'identify the family' item, run the two-question filter. Zygomorphic and papilionaceous? Fabaceae. Else: K + C, or tepals? Solanaceae versus Liliaceae.
Pro-tip: for economic-importance items, group by family. Fabaceae = pulses and oils; Solanaceae = food, spice, tobacco; Liliaceae = onion-garlic, Aloe, ornamentals.

segments.text: Let us close this subtopic with five pitfalls and two habits, and these are the last-mile ones, the errors that happen when you already know the material.

Pitfall one is mixing the three formulae, which is what happens when you learn them as three long strings. So do not. Anchor one signature word per family. Fabaceae equals diadelphous and papilionaceous. Solanaceae equals epipetalous and berry. Liliaceae equals tepals and epiphyllous.

Pitfall two is perianth versus calyx plus corolla. Liliaceae has one undifferentiated whorl, tepals, not separate calyx and corolla. Write K and C for a lily and you have described a different family.

Pitfall three is phylloclade versus phyllode. A phylloclade is a modified stem, as in Opuntia. A phyllode is a modified petiole or leaf, as in Acacia. Same green flattened look. Different organ. And you know how to check: stems carry nodes and buds.

Pitfall four is complete versus merous, and it is a fine one. Complete counts whorls, meaning all four present. Tri- or tetra- or penta-merous counts parts per whorl. Independent ideas, and a question can ask either without touching the other.

Pitfall five is a description written out of order, which is the saddest way to lose marks in this chapter, because you knew everything. Always habit, then vegetative, then floral, then fruit and seed. Per-field marking punishes a scrambled answer no matter how much correct biology is in it.

Now the first pro-tip, and it wins family questions in seconds. For any identify-the-family item, run the two-question filter. Zygomorphic with a papilionaceous corolla? Fabaceae, stop. Otherwise, distinct calyx and corolla, or tepals? That separates Solanaceae from Liliaceae.

And the second pro-tip, for economic-importance items, which are pure recall and therefore pure organisation. Group them by family. Fabaceae is pulses and oils. Solanaceae is food, spice, and tobacco. Liliaceae is onion and garlic, Aloe, and ornamentals. Three buckets, and every economic plant in the syllabus falls into one of them.
अब इस subtopic को बंद करते हैं पाँच pitfalls और दो habits के साथ — और ये आख़िरी मील वाली हैं, यानी वो ग़लतियाँ जो तब होती हैं जब material आपको पहले से आता है।

Pitfall one है तीनों formulae का घुल जाना, जो तब होता है जब आप उन्हें तीन लंबी लड़ियों की तरह सीखते हैं। तो मत सीखिए। हर family के लिए एक signature शब्द anchor कीजिए। Fabaceae यानी diadelphous और papilionaceous। Solanaceae यानी epipetalous और berry। Liliaceae यानी tepals और epiphyllous।

Pitfall two है perianth बनाम calyx plus corolla। Liliaceae में एक ही undifferentiated whorl है, tepals — अलग calyx और corolla नहीं। Lily के लिए K और C लिख दिया तो आपने किसी और family का description दे दिया।

Pitfall three है phylloclade बनाम phyllode। Phylloclade एक modified stem है, जैसे Opuntia में। Phyllode एक modified petiole या leaf है, जैसे Acacia में। वही हरा चपटा रूप। अलग organ। और जाँचना आपको आता है — stems पर nodes और buds होते हैं।

Pitfall four है complete बनाम merous, और ये बारीक है। Complete whorls गिनता है, यानी चारों मौजूद। Tri-, tetra- या penta-merous हर whorl में parts गिनता है। स्वतंत्र ideas, और question किसी एक को दूसरे को छुए बिना पूछ सकता है।

Pitfall five है क्रम से बाहर लिखी हुई description, जो इस chapter में marks गँवाने का सबसे दुखद तरीक़ा है — क्योंकि आपको सब आता था। हमेशा habit, फिर vegetative, फिर floral, फिर fruit और seed। Per-field marking बिखरे हुए जवाब को सज़ा देती है, चाहे उसमें कितनी भी सही biology भरी हो।

अब पहला pro-tip, और ये family के questions seconds में जिता देता है। किसी भी identify-the-family item के लिए दो सवालों वाला filter चलाइए। Zygomorphic और papilionaceous corolla? Fabaceae, रुक जाइए। वरना — अलग calyx और corolla, या tepals? यही Solanaceae को Liliaceae से अलग कर देता है।

और दूसरा pro-tip, economic-importance वाले items के लिए, जो पूरी तरह recall हैं और इसीलिए पूरी तरह व्यवस्था का खेल हैं। इन्हें family से बाँटिए। Fabaceae यानी pulses और oils। Solanaceae यानी food, spice, और tobacco। Liliaceae यानी onion-garlic, Aloe, और ornamentals। तीन डिब्बे, और syllabus का हर economic plant इन्हीं में से किसी एक में गिरता है।

board_events.text: ROOT vs STEM: root = descending, non-green, no nodes/internodes/buds, unicellular hairs, from radicle. Stem = ascending, green when young, has nodes/internodes/buds, from plumule.

Root systems: tap (dicot, mustard) · fibrous (monocot, wheat) · adventitious (banyan, grass, maize). Zones tip to base: root cap → meristematic → elongation → maturation (root hairs, absorption, lateral roots).

Root mods: storage (carrot, sweet potato) · prop (banyan) · stilt (sugarcane, maize) · pneumatophore (Rhizophora). Stem mods: rhizome-ginger · tuber-potato · tendril-cucurbits · thorn-Citrus. Leaf: base (±stipules) · petiole · lamina. Net = dicot, parallel = mono. Phyllotaxy: alternate (mustard) · opposite (guava) · whorled (Nerium).

FLOWER = modified shoot; four whorls on the thalamus: calyx, corolla (accessory) + androecium, gynoecium (essential). Inflorescence: racemose (axis grows, acropetal, mustard) vs cymose (axis ends in a flower, basipetal, Solanum). Symmetry: actinomorphic (mustard) · zygomorphic (pea) · asymmetric (Canna). Aestivation: valvate (Calotropis) · twisted (China rose) · imbricate (Cassia) · vexillary (pea).

Ovary position: hypogynous = superior (mustard) · perigynous = half-inferior (plum) · epigynous = inferior (guava). Placentation: marginal (pea) · axile (tomato) · parietal (mustard) · free central (Dianthus) · basal (sunflower). Ovary position → formula only; aestivation & placentation → diagram only.

Mapping: ovule → seed, ovary → fruit. Seed: coat (testa + tegmen), hilum, micropyle, embryo, endosperm (+ aleurone). Albuminous (maize) vs ex-albuminous (gram); perisperm (black pepper). Monocot grain: scutellum + coleoptile + coleorhiza. Fruit: epicarp → mesocarp → endocarp; true (mango) vs false (apple); parthenocarpic (banana); drupe = stony endocarp.

FAMILIES. Fabaceae: % ⚥ K(5) C1+2+(2) A(9)+1 G1 · papilionaceous · diadelphous · marginal · legume · pulses. Solanaceae: ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2) · epipetalous · axile · berry · potato/tomato. Liliaceae: ⊕ ⚥ P3+3 A3+3 G(3) · tepals · epiphyllous · axile · capsule · onion/Aloe.

MEMORY AIDS: 'Roots have no Nodes, no Buds.' · 'Net for Dicot, Parallel for Mono.' · 'Potato has eyes (stem), sweet potato is blind (root).' · 'Hypo-Super, Epi-Infer.' · 'Racemose Rises, Cymose Caps off.' · 'Epi-Meso-Endo, outside in.' · 'ex- = exit endosperm.' · 'Faba Fights, Solana Sticks, Lily Lifts tepals.'

segments.text: This is the whole chapter on one board. Do not learn anything new here. Use this to check that everything you already learned is still where you left it.

Start with the master map, because the chapter has a shape. Sub-one was the vegetative body. Sub-two was the flower. Sub-three was fruit and seed. And Sub-four was all of that vocabulary, put to work describing families.

Root versus stem, and it is still the hinge of the first subtopic. A root descends, is non-green, has no nodes, internodes or buds, has unicellular hairs, and comes from the radicle. A stem ascends, is green when young, has nodes, internodes and buds, and comes from the plumule.

Root systems: tap for dicots, mustard; fibrous for monocots, wheat; adventitious for banyan, grass and maize. And the zones, tip to base: root cap, meristematic, elongation, maturation, where the root hairs are and the absorption happens.

Modifications as triplets: storage, prop, stilt, pneumatophore for roots. Rhizome-ginger, tuber-potato, tendril-cucurbits, thorn-Citrus for stems. And for the leaf: base, petiole, lamina. Net for dicot, parallel for mono. Phyllotaxy alternate, opposite, whorled.

The flower is a modified shoot, with four whorls on the thalamus: calyx and corolla accessory, androecium and gynoecium essential. Inflorescence racemose or cymose. Symmetry, and aestivation, each with its plant attached.

Ovary position: hypogynous is superior, perigynous is half-inferior, epigynous is inferior. Placentation: marginal, axile, parietal, free central, basal. And the division of labour: ovary position from the formula only, aestivation and placentation from the diagram only.

Then the mapping that opened the third subtopic: ovule to seed, ovary to fruit. Seed coat, hilum, micropyle, embryo, endosperm. Albuminous against ex-albuminous. The monocot trio of scutellum, coleoptile, coleorhiza. Pericarp outside in. True, false, parthenocarpic, drupe.

And the three families, each as one line and one signature. Fabaceae: papilionaceous, diadelphous, marginal, legume. Solanaceae: epipetalous, axile, berry. Liliaceae: tepals, epiphyllous, axile, capsule.

<excited>And the memory aids, which are yours now. Roots have no nodes, no buds. Net for dicot, parallel for mono. Potato has eyes, so it is a stem; sweet potato is blind, so it is a root. Hypo-super, epi-infer. Racemose rises, cymose caps off. Epi-meso-endo, outside in. Ex- means exit endosperm. And Faba fights, Solana sticks, Lily lifts tepals. That is the chapter.
ये पूरा chapter एक ही board पर है। यहाँ कुछ नया मत सीखिए। इसका इस्तेमाल ये जाँचने के लिए कीजिए कि जो पहले सीखा था, वो अब भी अपनी जगह है या नहीं।

Master map से शुरू कीजिए, क्योंकि इस chapter की एक बनावट है। Sub-one vegetative body था। Sub-two flower। Sub-three fruit और seed। और Sub-four वही सारी शब्दावली, families describe करने के काम पर लगी हुई।

Root बनाम stem, और यही अब भी पहले subtopic का कब्ज़ा है। Root नीचे जाता है, non-green होता है, उसमें nodes, internodes या buds नहीं होते, hairs unicellular होते हैं, और वो radicle से आता है। Stem ऊपर जाता है, young में green होता है, उसमें nodes, internodes और buds होते हैं, और वो plumule से आता है।

Root systems — dicots के लिए tap, यानी mustard; monocots के लिए fibrous, यानी wheat; adventitious यानी banyan, grass और maize। और zones, tip से base तक — root cap, meristematic, elongation, maturation, जहाँ root hairs हैं और absorption होता है।

Modifications triplets की तरह — roots के लिए storage, prop, stilt, pneumatophore। Stems के लिए rhizome-ginger, tuber-potato, tendril-cucurbits, thorn-Citrus। और leaf के लिए — base, petiole, lamina। Net यानी dicot, parallel यानी mono। Phyllotaxy — alternate, opposite, whorled।

Flower एक modified shoot है, thalamus पर चार whorls के साथ — calyx और corolla accessory, androecium और gynoecium essential। Inflorescence racemose या cymose। Symmetry, और aestivation, हर एक अपने plant के साथ चिपका हुआ।

Ovary position — hypogynous यानी superior, perigynous यानी half-inferior, epigynous यानी inferior। Placentation — marginal, axile, parietal, free central, basal। और काम का बँटवारा — ovary position सिर्फ़ formula से, aestivation और placentation सिर्फ़ diagram से।

फिर वो mapping जिससे तीसरा subtopic खुला था — ovule से seed, ovary से fruit। Seed coat, hilum, micropyle, embryo, endosperm। Albuminous बनाम ex-albuminous। Monocot की तिकड़ी — scutellum, coleoptile, coleorhiza। Pericarp बाहर से अंदर। True, false, parthenocarpic, drupe।

और तीनों families, हर एक एक line और एक signature के साथ। Fabaceae — papilionaceous, diadelphous, marginal, legume। Solanaceae — epipetalous, axile, berry। Liliaceae — tepals, epiphyllous, axile, capsule।

<excited>और memory aids, जो अब आपके हैं। Roots में न nodes, न buds। Net for dicot, parallel for mono। Potato की आँखें हैं, तो वो stem है; sweet potato अंधा है, तो वो root है। Hypo-super, epi-infer। Racemose rises, cymose caps off। Epi-meso-endo, बाहर से अंदर। Ex- यानी exit endosperm। और Faba fights, Solana sticks, Lily lifts tepals। यही है पूरा chapter।
